subject: Request: Initial-frame SLAs and phased token-emission windows for hybrid endpoints

Subject: Request: Initial-frame SLAs and phased token-emission windows for hybrid endpoints

Hi Jasmine,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the hybrid endpoint concept looks promising for our low-latency trader chat use case. Before we proceed to pilot, we need to formalize an SLA carveout specifically addressing streaming vs non-streaming behavior. Two things are make-or-break for us: time-to-first-token (TTFT) and sustained token emission during sustained multi-second responses.

High-level ask: can Redwood commit to measurable TTFT and token/sec targets (or a documented carveout) for our hybrid endpoint? We're aware that eviction/warm-up and batching behaviors can vary across models and deployments; we want an explicit written exception (pilot carveout) that documents expected behavior and rollback conditions.

Example expectations from our side (open to negotiation):
- TTFT (first token): p95 <= 250ms for streaming endpoints for requests <= 1k tokens of context.
- Sustained throughput: baseline of 150 tokens/sec sustained with burst capacity to 300 tokens/sec for up to 10s for critical trade-update streams.
- If the streaming path is unavailable, auto-fallback to chunked/non-streaming must not exceed 1s additional head latency.

We attached the GreenBank security Q&A and a redline-friendly SLA draft (redwood-sla-draft-v3.pdf). Please confirm whether these targets are feasible for a 90-day pilot, or propose alternative numeric bands with clear metrics and monitoring.

We'd like a written carveout included in the MSA addendum so our trading engineers can instrument against the agreed metrics.

Thanks,
Alex

Alex — thanks for the clear ask and the attachments. I looped in Ben (sales) and Karthik (infra) to scope feasibility. A couple of quick clarifying questions before we workshop numbers:

1) Traffic profile: are the majority of calls short (responses < 200 tokens) or long (multi-k token transcripts)? Do bursts come from many concurrent sockets or from a handful of large responses?
2) When you say “300 tokens/sec for up to 10s,” is that a strict requirement for every single connection or an aggregate across dedicated capacity?

Our current thinking (provisional) — and this is what we want to validate with infra: we can offer a phased pilot carveout that specifies:
- An initial-frame (first token) commitment with slightly relaxed bands on hosted vs dedicated.
- A sustained emission window with two tiers: baseline sustained rate for standard capacity, and a burst window for dedicated/D2D allocations.

Can you provide a short sample trace (one representative request) with timestamps if possible, and the expected SLA priority (blocker vs target for pilot)? We'll incorporate specific telemetry hooks in the SLA draft so both sides can verify.

Quick next step: can we schedule a 30-minute technical sync with your SREs and our infra (Karthik) tomorrow?

—Jasmine

Alex — appreciate the crisp ask. Following an internal run with infra, here is a concrete proposal we can offer for the 90-day pilot (numbers negotiable):

Proposal (Pilot, 90 days):
- Platform: Hybrid endpoint (streaming-first, fallback to chunked).
- TTFT: Dedicated capacity: p95 <= 350ms for first token (models up to 30B). Hosted (shared): p95 <= 500ms; longer for >30B models (we'll document per-model bands).
- Sustained throughput: Baseline sustained emission of 60 tokens/sec per connection.
- Burst window: Ability to provision bursts up to 200 tokens/sec per connection for up to 8s when Dedicated capacity is reserved (burst subject to advance booking via our Capacity API).
- Fallback behavior: If streaming path is constrained (queueing or KV-cache miss), requests will fallback to non-streaming chunked delivery after a 12s soft timeout. In such cases, TTFT for the non-streaming chunked response may see an additional 700–900ms overhead depending on model size.
- Credits: If we miss dedicated TTFT p95 >350ms more than 3 times in a billing month for production-labeled endpoints, we will issue a 10% credit for that month (subject to verification).

Notes: these numbers are conservative relative to your ask; they reflect observed behavior under our current batching and KV-warmup model for long-context workloads. To tighten bands we recommend a Dedicated reservation (Redwood Dedicated) and a brief warmup run against a representative prompt set so caches warm and kernels JIT.

Next steps:
- Tech sync today/tomorrow to align on traces.
- If acceptable, we’ll produce an SLA addendum that includes the agreed thresholds, instrumentation (Prometheus metrics + trace IDs), and a rollback clause at the end of pilot.

Ben/Jasmine — quick technical context to accompany the proposal above so legal/ops know what we can instrument for verification:

1) Why numbers differ by hosted vs dedicated:
   - On shared/hosted nodes we operate multi-tenant batching and ephemeral GKVs; TTFT variance increases due to queueing/prefetch limits. Dedicated pools allow reserved KV cache residency and predictable scheduler slots.

2) Primary failure modes that affect TTFT and token/sec:
   - KV cache cold miss leading to an extra model load path (100-400ms penalty depending on weights on disk).
   - Kernel JIT activity for rarely-used attention patterns (warm-up can add 150-300ms on first requests).
   - Continuous batching: higher concurrency can increase TTFT while improving overall throughput.

3) What we can expose in the SLA for verification:
   - Per-request <trace_id>able metrics: first_token_latency_ms, sustained_tokens_per_sec_windowed (1s/5s/10s), model_variant_id, node_pool_id, fallback_reason (if any).
   - Prometheus-exported histograms and a pre-built Grafana dashboard template (we'll give read-only links).

4) Suggested rollout and metrics:
   - Pilot: run 1 week of perf tests with representative traces to calibrate dedicated reservation sizes.
   - Canary traffic: 2% traffic ramp over 48h with close monitoring of first_token_latency p50/p95/p99 and sustained tokens/sec distributions.

I'll draft a short instrumentation appendix to include with the SLA addendum (how to validate a breach, required evidence, sample queries).

Thanks — this is exactly the kind of specificity we needed. A few brief points and acceptance for pilot: 

1) Pilot acceptance: GreenBank accepts the 90-day pilot with the proposed bands (Dedicated p95 TTFT <= 350ms; baseline sustained 60 tokens/sec; bursts up to 200 tokens/sec for 8s), conditional on the following being added to the SLA addendum:
   - Pilot duration: 90 days from the first production-labeled request hitting the Dedicated pool.
   - Monthly reporting: Redwood provides a monthly perf report (p50/p95/p99 TTFT, count of fallback events, sustained token/sec distribution).
   - Rollback clause: If dedicated p95 TTFT > 350ms for 2 consecutive weeks AND fallback events exceed 0.5% of requests, GreenBank can pause the pilot and require remediation.

2) Evidence: We agree to use the traceable metrics you listed. Please include sample Prometheus queries in the instrumentation appendix so our SREs can validate.

3) Next step: Jasmine — go ahead and produce the SLA addendum with the instrumentation appendix and the booking process for burst reservations. We'll review and get legal to sign. Karthik — please include the Grafana read-only link and the exact label names we'll query.

Appreciate the quick turnaround and pragmatic numbers. Looking forward to the pilot.

—Alex
